title: OECD.AI Policy Observatory: OECD landing page on AI policy
answer: This is the OECD.AI Policy Observatory landing page from the OECD. It says the observatory helps countries shape trustworthy AI with the OECD AI Principles and gives access to 900+ national AI policies and initiatives, live data about AI and a blog about AI policy. It also notes that organisations developing advanced AI systems can submit reports to support transparency and comparability of risk mitigation measures, and that GPAI and OECD member countries' AI work formed an integrated partnership under the GPAI brand.

sections.body: The OECD publishes this page, which is the landing page for the OECD Artificial Intelligence Policy Observatory, also called OECD.AI. It presents the observatory as a source of access to 900+ national AI policies and initiatives, live data about AI and a blog about AI policy. It also describes participation by organisations developing advanced AI systems and a partnership involving GPAI and OECD member countries. The text states no publication date and is an overview rather than a detailed report.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The source says OECD.AI helps countries and shape trustworthy AI with the OECD AI Principles. It gives access to 900+ national AI policies and initiatives, live data about AI and a blog about AI policy. It states that organisations developing advanced AI systems can participate by submitting a report. By sharing information, the text says, they will facilitate transparency and comparability of risk mitigation measures. The source also says the GPAI initiative and OECD member countries' work on AI joined forces under the GPAI brand to create an integrated partnership. Its stated aim is to help AI actors develop and use trustworthy AI systems and applications that respect human rights and are fair, transparent, explainable, robust, secure and safe. The page does not describe individual policies, countries or data sets. It does not explain how the observatory collects or updates the 900+ policies and initiatives. It does not give a publication date. It presents the observatory as a policy resource and a participation route for advanced AI organisations, with the OECD AI Principles as the stated basis for trustworthy AI.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The source states 900+ national AI policies and initiatives. It names the OECD AI Principles as the basis for trustworthy AI. It lists human rights, fairness, transparency, explainability, robustness, security and safety as characteristics of trustworthy AI systems and applications. It says organisations developing advanced AI systems can submit a report to facilitate transparency and comparability of risk mitigation measures. It says the GPAI initiative and OECD member countries' work on AI joined forces under the GPAI brand to create an integrated partnership. It gives no other numbers.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in Government can use this source as an entry point to the OECD.AI Policy Observatory, which the source says provides access to 900+ national AI policies and initiatives, live data about AI and a blog about AI policy. It also points to the OECD AI Principles and a GPAI partnership, which are relevant to cross-country policy and governance discussions. The source is useful for locating comparative policy material and for understanding the observatory's stated role in supporting trustworthy AI. It does not itself provide detailed government case studies, procurement guidance or implementation evidence, so it is best treated as a signpost to further OECD.AI resources.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Government

sections.body: This is a short landing page with little substance. It does not name specific countries, policies or strategies, and it does not explain how the 900+ policies and initiatives are selected, classified or updated. It gives no publication date and no methodology. It does not cover public-sector implementation, procurement or outcomes. It is an overview from the OECD, not a commercial vendor page, but it is partial and high-level. The text also does not detail the report submission process or how the GPAI partnership operates.
